characters.name: In General
characters.description: The main antagonist, anunimaginably powerful AI computer virusof unknown origin. It is key to the operation of Disassembly Drones. The Absolute Solver can manipulate matter on the molecular level, creating virtually anything it desires out of thin air. When a drone "host" is destroyed, it begins to scavenge its surroundings for new materials to rebuild it — with horrifying results. It is also responsible for giving Doll, Uzi, and other infected Drones telekinetic abilities anda craving for oil. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: It's left ambiguous what the Solver actuallyis, but it's digital in presentation and a threat to both drones and humans alike.Assuming the humans made it, then the fact that it's called a "Solver" implies that it was supposed to serve agoodpurpose by helping to fix things, but due to its overwhelming power and lack of a moral code, ended up going haywire and becoming the monstrous being that it's known as instead.But, on the other hand, assuming it's not made by humanity turns the Solver into anOutside-Context Problemas literallyno-onewould have been able to consider it being a thing, let alone it being an issue to worry about. The fact that Patch 2.1.8 only seems to cover the digital side of things (i.e. prevents possessions but not physical changes or empowerment) for those infected with it only further emphasizes this alongside the "Uzi, Host of the Solver" acrylic outright calling it an Eternal Entity in the description. characters.name: Worker Drones
characters.description: A legion of worker robots built to serve humanity. Some of them formed their own society after a freak accident wiped out all humans on the exoplanet Copper 9, but were forced into hiding when their company sent the Disassembly Drones to slaughter them all. Actual Pacifist:Downplayed, as the Outpost 3 drones tend to not resort to violence in dangerous situations seems to stem more from them being not too bright, not helped by Khan's claims that they won't ever need to fight with his doors keeping the Disassembly Drones out, which doesn't really help when they're actually attacked. They're not against these violent methods, however, as they congratulateUzifor standing up to and utterly decimating J. Aerith and Bob: There are Worker Drones with normal-sounding names such as Thad, Khan, and Lizzy.Uzidoesn't sound too weird, but there's also one named Doll. A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Subverted. At the beginning of the Pilot, Uzi says that JC Jenson considered the Worker Drones of Copper-9 runaway A.I. and therefore should be killed before they begin to rebel for real. As it turns out, the Worker Drones aren’t particularly aggressive robots and would rather hide than fight (except for Uzi). Bespectacled Cutie: Some Worker Drones wear glasses and areCute Machines.

characters.name: Disassembly Drones (a.k.a. Murder Drones)
characters.description: A type of Drone created byJCJenson,except not really, designed to exterminate the Workers on Copper 9. Also known as Murder Drones by the WD population of Copper 9 and Sky Demons by Nori. Achilles' Heel:Despite seemingly nigh-unstoppable, Disassembly Drones do have weaknesses, most of which seem to be inspired by vampiric lore; at first a seeminglyInvokedbyJCJenson,Word of Godconfirms that the Disassembly Drones were designed as inefficiently temperature-wise as possible so that they'll quickly overheatonce there are no more Workers to kill. As a result, they run so hot that justtouchingone of them is liable to get you burned—if you're a human, that is—constantly need oil to survive and possess lethal sensitivity to sunlight. The actual perpetrator behind this weakness, going by "Dead End" andLiam Vickersconfirming the validity of Tessa's claims in said episode, appears to be the Absolute Solver.Aside from these, they also feel pain, and they can be affected by their own nanites (until they counteract it with their saliva), and destroying their hearts prevents immediate regeneration. As a result, they run so hot that justtouchingone of them is liable to get you burned—if you're a human, that is—constantly need oil to survive and possess lethal sensitivity to sunlight. The actual perpetrator behind this weakness, going by "Dead End" andLiam Vickersconfirming the validity of Tessa's claims in said episode, appears to be the Absolute Solver. Aside from these, they also feel pain, and they can be affected by their own nanites (until they counteract it with their saliva), and destroying their hearts prevents immediate regeneration.

characters.name: Zombie Drones
characters.description: Back from the Dead: These Workers have rebooted from software death after being disassembled. The Dreaded: They are this toJCJensonwho have an entire training video dedicated to the dangers that Zombie Drones can pose. With the Solver mutating in Zombie Drones such as Cyn, it's not hard to see why. Elite Zombie: Solver-infected Zombie Drones are this, having full access to its reality-warping powers. Face–Monster Turn: Following the Gala Massacre, they were all turned through unknown means into the Disassembly Drones. Night of the Living Mooks: The Elliot Manor Zombie Drones were turned into the Disassembly Drones supposedly by the Absolute Solver and sent to Copper-9 to accomplish its goals.

characters.name: Anti-Drone Sentinels
characters.description: Fast and deadly robots in the shape of velociraptors built byJCJensonto serve as security for the Cabin Fever labs on Copper 9. The Sentinels come equipped with stun flashers capable of locking Worker or Disassembly Drones in a "Boot Loop" which leaves them easy prey for their claws. Basilisk and Cockatrice: They take after basilisks, being reptilian creatures that can paralyze people with direct eye contact. Blinding Camera Flash: Their most potent weapon is a stunning flash that puts Drones into a boot loop, rendering them utterly helpless. Boring Yet Practical: On paper, they shouldn't hold a candle to the likes of Disassembly Drones; however, their anti-drone flasher works equally well against Disassembly Drones and Worker Drones, which allowed the Sentinels to utterly slaughter the previous squads that attempted to access Cabin Fever labs. Early-Bird Cameo: They appear as one of the deceased Test Subject's drawings in "Cabin Fever".

characters.name: Teacher
characters.description: Uzi's nameless and apathetic homeroom teacher. Ambiguously Related: In episode 3, after it’s announced that V became prom queen by forfeit because Doll killed all of the other candidates, and Lizzy explains that they are friends now and that V isn’t interested in killing anyone anymore, she threatens to get her dad to dock the other students’ grades if they don’t accept V taking part in the prom. This implies that her dad works as a teacher at the Outpost 3 School. Considering that The Teacher is the only teacher we see in the school and is implied to be the only one, it’s somewhat likely that she is his daughter. Apathetic Teacher:When at a parent-teacher conference with Khan, he's shown playing Solitaire in his heads-up display, even as Khan is yelling at him for calling Uzi "damaged."Doesn't show any notable emotion in "Cabin Fever" when V openly admits to eating some of his students (although it was really Uzi that killed most of them).When the Absolute Solver starts tearing apart the planet in "Absolute End", he's currently occupied grading his students, having just given Uzi an A- for "strong thesis + effective syntax" and an "amazing introductory paragraph & impressive summation of core case studies" on a paper titled "DUMB ESSAY STUPID" that is just the phrase "I AM GOD"repeated ad nauseam all over the page. He then takes a break from the grading to observe the apocalypse going on outside with bored annoyance, only escalating to mild indignation when one of the glowing energy tentacles of the Solver takes time out from destroying the planet to slap him across the face.By the end of the series, it seems that all of the nonsense is slowly getting to him, as he's last seen repeatedly banging his head against his desk as Uzi's giving her presentation. When at a parent-teacher conference with Khan, he's shown playing Solitaire in his heads-up display, even as Khan is yelling at him for calling Uzi "damaged." characters.name: Lizzy
characters.description: A preppy Worker Drone girl who bullies Uzi. Adaptational Jerkass: Downplayed in that Lizzy was never a nice person in the original series, but the comic has her lacking one of her kinder moments in which she goes out of her way to risk herself to protect V from Doll, and later fixes the former and N. By contrast, Lizzy in the comic abandons V when Doll starts attacking her with her Solver. All Girls Want Bad Boys: A rare same-sex variant (largely, seeAmbiguously Bi), but she still embodies the general implications of this trope, seeing as how the only drones she’s shown genuine attraction towards are cannibals who have no issue with killing people. Alpha Bitch: Her being a school student who ruthlessly bullies people she doesn't like gives off this vibe. Ambiguously Bi: She calls V "hotter than Doll" and tries to warn her of Doll's attack. The finale implies even further that she had feelings for Doll, with her hosting Doll's funeral, where she tellingly calls her 'BABE-A-TRON QUEENTHOUSAND' and says she wishes another classmate had died instead. On another occasion she called the male N's defiance and chewing out of V hot in "Cabin Fever", backtracking only after getting a glare from V.

characters.name: Doll
characters.description: One of Uzi's classmates. A reserved Worker Drone who inexplicably speaks Russian. There's more to her than meets the eye. Achilles' Heel: Despite her powers, it doesn't actually take much to take her down if you're able to catch her off guard... or if you're immune to the Absolute Solver's matter manipulation. Alas, Poor Villain: Her fate is to be eaten by Tessa’s corpse. All her efforts, trying to find a cure for it and trying to stop the Solver from fully reaching Copper-9, have all been in vain, and now she is going to be eaten by a beast. The expression on her face just hammers this down. All for Nothing: Completely fails in her goal of exorcising the Solver from her body and is killed by it. The Aloner: Although she hangs out with Lizzy, Doll usually prefers to be alone. This is pretty much herFatal Flawwhich gets her killed by the Absolute Solver.

characters.name: Thad
characters.description: One of Uzi's classmates in Outpost 3, a friendly jock Worker Drone and one of the few to treat Uzi with any sort of respect. Action Survivor: Gets brutally attacked by V, but survives without being crippled. Also survives nearly being eaten by the Absolute Solver. Adaptation Name Change: Subverted. In the early releases of the graphic novel adaptation, Thad's name was changed toChad. Though it's fixed with the later releases. Chekhov's Skill: Routinely returns Uzi's railgun to her throughout the series and does so one last time inAbsolute End, giving her a weapon to begin the fight against Cyn and J with. Dare to Be Badass: With the Murder Drones closing in, Thad picks up a pipe and tries to convince Khan to help fight back, reminding him that it's his duty to defend. Unfortunately, Khan turns out to be such aDirty Cowardthat he wouldn't even try, resulting in Thad getting thrashed and nearly killed by V before Uzi and N pull aBig Damn Heroes.He later shows in "Mass Destruction" with Lizzy and Khan, who lead them to the Cabin Fever Labs when the planet's gravity starts to distort. Last we see them, he and Lizzy are preparing to fight J head-on.

characters.name: Ronathan
characters.description: The bus driver for Outpost 3 School. Cowboy: Has this look. Custom Uniform: Doesn't have the traditional bus drivers' uniform, instead wears a jacket and a cowboy hat and boots. The Driver: See his character description. My Horse Is a Motorbike: Inverted. His school bus acts like a horse.

characters.name: Other Outpost  3 Students
characters.description: Apathetic Citizens: They don't seem to care when other students die, only if their life is directly in danger, that or they'redesensitized to seeing others be murdered at this point. One-Shot Character: More than a few of them are this as they get brutally killed off in the episode that they debut in. Red Shirt: They largely exist to be brutally killed off. Vague Age: It's not clear how exactly old they are, despite acting like high school teens, withWord of Godstating that they're in their "older teens" (16-19), never mind that Copper 9's calendar system isn't the same as Earth's. An unseen male Worker Drone who is Rebecca's date to the prom.

characters.name: WDF as a Whole
characters.description: A defence force of Worker Drones in charge of building the giant doors that keep the Disassembly Drones out. Crippling Overspecialization: While Khan's engineering skills do allow the WDF to build doors capable of keeping the Disassembly Drones out, it's theironlymethod to do so. Once the Disassembly Drones managed to get past them, then they had very little to nothing to fall back on, aside from Khan hopefully closing the next door. Demoted to Extra: In the graphic novel adaptation, Braxton, Makarov, Todd, and the Unnamed Worker Defense Force Member are killed by N before Uzi could get back to Outpost 3. Hero of Another Story: On Khan's certificate, it states that the WDF of Outpost 9 gave him that certificate, revealing that there are other divisions of the WDF in other Outposts dealing with other Disassembly Drone teams. The Pirates Who Don't Do Anything: The Worker Defense Force, or at least the Outpost 3 WDF, is supposed to, well,defendagainst Murder Drones. However, they are so reliant on the doors Khan built to protect everybody that they don't do much else besides sit around and play cards. The moment the Murder Drones manage to break in, and people expect them to defend, they all simply run and cower in fear. Subverted with Khan in "Mass Destruction", who repairs Uzi's railgun and leads Lizzy and Thad to confront J at Camp 98.7.

characters.name: Khan
characters.description: Uzi's respected yet cowardly father and head of the Outpost 3 WDF. He really, really,reallyloves doors. Abusive Parents: He's emotionally abusive towards Uzi and prefers doors over her.A few bits of text on the newsintroducing him earlier in "Pilot" shows him saying"Doors are my real daughter"and calling Uzi a"disappointing failure"on public media. Later episodes after hisCharacter Developmenthave him openly admit that he's not very good at being a parent, but he's trying to be there more for Uzi. Actual Pacifist: Only relies on doors for protection,which becomes a problem once the Murder Drones actually get inside. It might have to do with a past trauma from having toMercy Killhis wife. Adaptational Jerkass: In the graphic novel adaptation, Khan's decision to leave Uzi for dead when N took her hostage is notably more callous and unsympathetic. In the original show, he does so with some reluctance, and it's somewhat understandable given his traumatic fear of the Dissassembly Drones and being unlikely to save his daughter due to his lack of aiming skills and N being just too fast. In the graphic novel adaptation, Khan simply runs away without hesitation. Adaptational Nice Guy: That said, Khan attempts to be a better father to Uzi quicker than in the series, as his talk with the teacher convinced him that he could be able to still fix the neglect he did towards his daughter and leaving her for dead "once", and actually gives comforting words to Uzi when he sees her after the latter, and N defeated the Solver.

characters.name: Other Members
characters.description: All There in the Script: His name is only mentioned in the end credits. Half the Man He Used to Be: Gets bisected by N's laser. His Name Is...: Tries to introduce himself to Uzi when they're both running from N. Screw This, I'm Outta Here: Tries to run from N along with the other WDF drones. The Outpost 3 detective who investigates Tim's murder.

characters.name: Nori
characters.description: Uzi's mother and Khan's wife. Ambiguously Evil: "Dead End" implies that Nori might have intentionally left Alice and the other Cabin Fever test subjects to die and may have also been the one who destroyed Copper 9's core, which killed all the humans on the planet. The ambiguous part comes from the question of the extent to which Nori was in control of herself versus being a puppet of the Absolute Solver, as she had gold eyes in the video that Tessa shows N, indicating that she was possessed by the Absolute Solver. "Mass Destruction" makes clear that shewasn'tin control of herself, the Solver was, and she's not only stillalive, but actively fighting the Solver, conscripting N into helping her when they meet. Ambiguous Situation: It's unknown justwhichof the three Disassembly Drones was responsible for damaging Nori to the point that Khan was forced toMercy Killher. Her comment that N looks familiar to her indicates it was him who was responsible, though it could equally be that she remembered him from the three Disassembly Drones attacking Outpost 3 in general. Amnesiac Dissonance:Implied, as she tells N that, following the core collapse, her memories were scrambled enough to "have a kid", implying she normally wouldn't have fallen in love with Khan and had Uzi were it not for her missing memories (especially considering that the kid would inherit the Solver). Considering her default personality is very much like Uzi's, her being atsundereabout it definitely would fit, as while she calls Khan a "hunk" and clearly cares about Uzi, she more than likely wouldn't admit it outright. Her actions upon reuniting with Khan in "Absolute End" confirm this.Khan:Uh... Tha —Nori:YOU DON'T KNOW ME AND I HATE YOU![scurries away bawling] Apocalypse Maiden: Comes with the territory of being a host of the Absolute Solver.

characters.name: Yeva
characters.description: Doll's mother and another Drone with the Absolute Solver. Apocalypse Maiden: Comes with the territory of being a host of the Absolute Solver. Best Friend: To Nori, asWord of Godstates that they were close friends and the "ultimate gamer team". Big Damn Heroes: She saves Mitch from being killed by the Solver-possessed Nori, and then herself and the latter once the Core Collapses. Deader than Dead: Despite being a patched Worker Drone with the powers of the Absolute Solver, Yeva'sKilled Off for Realby V in the past due to her core also being destroyed.

characters.name: Alice
characters.description: Abusive Parents: She's essentially Beau's guardian, and not only did she groom him to be a sadisticSerial Killerlike her, but she also verbally abuses him quite frequently. Keep in mind that Beau is the Worker Drone equivalent of atoddler. Adaptational Nice Guy:Downplayedas she still isn't shown to care for them, but in the graphic novel adaptation, she lacks her scenes where she is verbally abusive to Beau. Animal Motifs:Downplayed. Alice, as if she wasn't unsettling enough, engages in unnatural behavior similar to a four-legged animal, though it's not directly clear which creature she represents.She possesses a makeshift Disassembly Drone-inspired tail, bounces from objects on all-fours, perches on tabletops,is always barefoot,never removes her feet from the chair, and always preys on whoever stumbles in her territory, includingthe dreaded Disassembly Drones. These traits are comparable to cats who typically sit on furniture, hop from object-to-object, and are natural born hunters.Unlike most Worker Drones, Alice dons crafted antlers on her hardhat consisting of various scraps that were most likely scattered around the facility. These horns are creepily reminiscent of deer antlers. Incredibly ironic considering deers are symbolized as gentle, innocent, and meek creatures, and Alice herself is asadistic psychopath who murders and harvests her victims. characters.name: Beau
characters.description: A baby Worker Drone with Disassembly Drone parts grafted onto his body who serves as Alice's minion. Adaptational Villainy: The graphic novel adaptation has him being killed alongside Alice by the Sentinels, rather than dying performing aHeroic Sacrificeto save V. Affably Evil: Beau is quite friendly to his victims, particularly N, in a much more genuine manner thanAlice. Ambiguous Situation: It's unclear what or who Beau actually is. Is he a creation of Alice or another test subject? Anti-Villain: Beau's a crazed serial killer, but he ultimately decides to free V at the cost of his own life.

characters.name: Amda
characters.description: A Worker Drone that is killed by the Sentinels. Chronic Hero Syndrome: Tries to get one of her fellow Worker Drones to safety despite the Sentinels on the prowl, but they both end up being eaten by the Sentinels. No Name Given: Her actual name goes unmentioned. Averted in "Mass Destruction" when we get or at least a Drone that shares her number's name. Off with His Head!: Her corpse ends up suffering this at the hands of Alice. Victim of the Week: Is killed by theMonster of the Week.

characters.name: Deceased Test Subject
characters.description: Escaped from the Lab: It appeared that they tried to do so and managed to partially succeed before they died. I Warned You: A posthumous example. They wrote a warning to someone, telling them to not to "look for answers". From what Uzi, N and V go through while trying to learn more about the Absolute Solver, they were right. Mad Artist: The drawings that are found with them...are disturbing to say the least. Memento MacGuffin: Like Nori, Yeva and other Solver-Infected Test Subjects, they wear a skull choker. No Name Given: They remain unnamed.

characters.name: Doll's Father
characters.description: A Worker Drone who is the father of Doll and husband of Yeva. He was killed by V at one point along with his wife. Ambiguous Situation:"Dead End" implies that, like his wife, he was infected by the Absolute Solver, as Tessa mentions that Doll thinks that the Cabin Fever Labs scientists did something to her parents and gave them a sickness that she inherited, which is the Absolute Solver, implying both of them were infected. Though unlike Nori and Yeva,he doesn't have a skull choker as they do, so his infected status is still up in the air. But given that "Tessa" is really Cyn, it's possible that he wasn't infected at all.It's unclear why he took a snapshot of V right before his death. At first, it can be assumed that Doll's father decided to take a picture of V when it was clear he wouldn't make it out alive, to give the rest of any surviving Worker Drones the identity of his killer if they came across his body. However, with the reveal of his wife being part of the experiments with the Absolute Solver, it's also possible that he was trying to recreate the Anti-Drone Sentinels'Blinding Camera Flashto incapacitate V. "Dead End" implies that, like his wife, he was infected by the Absolute Solver, as Tessa mentions that Doll thinks that the Cabin Fever Labs scientists did something to her parents and gave them a sickness that she inherited, which is the Absolute Solver, implying both of them were infected. Though unlike Nori and Yeva,he doesn't have a skull choker as they do, so his infected status is still up in the air. But given that "Tessa" is really Cyn, it's possible that he wasn't infected at all. It's unclear why he took a snapshot of V right before his death. characters.name: Frank
characters.description: A repairman who gets assigned to repair the hole in the roof. Oh, Crap!: Panics when Eldritch J appears. One-Shot Character: Only appears in "Heartbeat". Scream Discretion Shot: The scene cuts away as he screams. This Is Gonna Suck: Has this reaction to being assigned to fix the hole in the roof.

characters.name: Grant
characters.description: A Worker Drone who was ambushed by V along with his family and killed sometime before the Pilot. All There in the Script: His name is only mentioned in the end credits. Cruel and Unusual Death: Based off the dialogue in his death scene, Vripped out and force fed him his own entrailsas his family watched before murdering them all. Flat Character: Only appears in one scene and is used to show V's sadism. I Have a Family: Pleads for V to not feed him his own entrails in front of his own family.

characters.name: Reid
characters.description: A Worker Drone who is outside when Tessa and J arrive. All There in the Script: His name is only mentioned in the end credits. Flat Character: Any personality traits that make him a notable character is completely obscure, only having one line within his entire role before facing his inevitable death to officially announce Tessa's.Justified, since he's a mereOne-Shot Character. I Need to Go Iron My Dog: When he finds his glasses, he claims that he found "his excuse to be outside." Off with His Head!: Gets his head chopped off by Tessa.

characters.name: Uzi
characters.description: The main protagonist, an angsty teenage Worker Drone from Outpost 3 who'd rather fight the killer robots hunting her fellow drones than hide from them. After forming an unlikely bond with N, she plotted to escape Copper 9 and tear humanity a new one… but outside forces soon get in the way of that goal, and she ends up drawn into a mystery that changes her in more ways than one. Aborted Arc:Downplayed.The "Pilot" ends with her deciding to invade Earth andKill All Humansas revenge for their siccing the Disassembly Drones on Copper 9, suggesting she's going to become aVillain Protagonist. She initially intends on making due on this plan in the next episode, even excusing that if the Disassembly Drones' Pod doesn't have functioning communications then the humans aren't interested in talking anyway. But, with N pointing out that if comms weren't working thensomeonemust have been giving orders to J, Uzi slows down enough to actually think about her plan, and realize what's going on hereof course isn't as simple and black-and-white as she has initially assumed, and ends up dropping her "Kill All Humans" plan in favor of the more focused, and much more reasonable"Kill J's Boss"plan instead. Albeit begrudgingly.Uzi:Quit complicating my murder plan. Action Girl: In heavy contrast to the rest of the Worker Drones at Outpost 3, who for some reason can't bring themselves to fight back against the Murder Drones. She has a small degree of skill in martial arts from just watching anime, and she's applauded for managing to take out J by herself. Adaptational Badass: In the official comic adaptation, Uzi manages to block N's nanite acid tail stab to her face out of reflex and take down J without getting hit with theEMP. All-Loving Hero: Surprisingly, despite how surly and prickly she usually is, she shows shades of this several times. She's genuinely angered thatJCJensonseems to have given their Disassembly Drones no way off Copper 9 once their job is done and passionately explains t

characters.name: The Keybug
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: It gets caught in a tug-of-war between Uzi and Doll, it is kidnapped by Doll, twice and finally when Tessa briefly gets it back, she spins it on her finger, making the poor roach sick. And then Doll squashes it into the panel opening the way to the secret lab. Cyber Green: It has green glowing lights. Dropped a Bridge on Him: When Doll snatches it from Tessa in the Cabin Fever Labs, she activates the secret elevator by smashing the Keybug into the panel.It gets better.Keybug:[bruh.jpg] 💀 Gold-Colored Superiority: Unlike its fellow roaches, it is golden and has a higher plot relevance. Living MacGuffin: Seems to be this as it's a key part of the mystery surrounding the Cabin Fever Labs.

characters.name: Sparky
characters.description: All There in the Manual: The name Sparky is given to it in social media. Defeat Equals Friendship: V manages to best it offscreen and it becomes her loyal mount in turn. Elite Mook: They demonstrate a higher degree of intelligence than its blue-eyed brethren. It knows how to use severed drone limbs' weapons against V and fights her solo. Expy: As a velociraptor that was tamed and helps the protagonists, Sparky is one toBlue. Ironic, considering the eye-colour that denotes their difference to other Sentinels. Grew Beyond Their Programming: Thanks to a combination of experiencing aLogic Bombfrom thinking that "Tessa's" a drone but also seeing her bleed and then knocking itself out when it hits a wall, it ends up rebooting in a damaged state that allows it to bypass it's "don't hurt humans" rule when Tessa attempts to confuse it with her blood again, and begin utilizing a severed Disassembly Drone's arm as a weapon. It would later end up deciding to join V offscreen after the latter attempted aHeroic Sacrificedespite it being programmed to target drones. Although it's initially aggressive with Lizzy in the finale, it never uses any lethal force and would eventually stop bothering her as indicated in the end credits.

characters.name: JCJensonas a Whole
characters.description: TheMegaCorpresponsible for the existence of the Drones and the overarching antagonists of the series. Complexity Addiction: They at least seem to be afflicted with this.Restraining Boltsor evena few well-placed missileswould probably be a more efficient way to relieve their concerns about the Copper 9 Worker Dronesbecoming independent, but apparently constructing a series of vampiricMechanical Abominationsin the form of the Disassembly Drones to slowly kill off the Workers over a period of several years was a much better idea.Although it's possible they have goals beyond simply wiping out the workers, specifically recovering the secretive, disturbing research which seems to have involved the Absolute Solver and its reality-warping potential.Bombarding the supposedly empty and written-off planet from space with enough firepower to wipe out underground shelters could cause too many eyebrows to be raised and attract too much attention. Sending a couple of "disassembly drones" to "disassemble some malfunctioning automatics" would be much more plausible."Dead End" (and Liam Vickers on Glitch X 2023) finally reveals the truth: the Disassembly Drones aren't related toJCJensonat all, but are instead minions of the Absolute Solver, instructed to kill all life on exoplanets they land on and seek out the research the Copper 9 scientists were conducting into it. That said, their chosen security bots are stillrobot velociraptors!Granted, said robot velociraptors killed every single Disassembly Drone sent after them, so it seems likeJCJensonwas onto something with that design. Although it's possible they have goals beyond simply wiping out the workers, specifically recovering the secretive, disturbing research which seems to have involved the Absolute Solver and its reality-warping potential. Bombarding the supposedly empty and written-off planet from space with enough firepower to wipe out underground shelters could cause too many eyebrows to be raised and attract too much atten

characters.name: Tessa
characters.description: An AustralianJCJensontechnician who comes to Copper 9 for "maintenance work". Abusive Parents: From what we can see in N's memories, her treating drones as if they were people didn't exactly put her on good terms with her parents - to the point that they chained her up when she wouldn't throw them out. Ambiguously Bi: Alongside being AmbiguouslyRobosexual, she calls N "tall and handsome" when they first meet up, but this ends up being Cyn in disguise. She also asks J to pretend to be a "rippling hot royal stud" to help her prepare for socializing at the Gala and playfully flirts with her.If nothing else, her voice actress, Daisy Rosesupports the idea that Tessa might've had romantic feelings for J. Ambiguously Brown: Most of her skin is notably darker than "white", but still several tones lighter than "black", but she has areas of much darker skin around her eyes, and her hair is completely straight. Given that decay causes the skin to become paler and to change colour somewhat, topped with her skin only being seen when she is a corpse, it is ultimately impossible to pin her down to any one race. Ambiguously Human: While it could be excused as the result ofTraining from Hellup until she arrived on Copper 9 at the end of "The Promening", Tessa demonstrated to be far stronger and faster for a human, especially when her space suit gets punctured but still functions normally despite the toxic atmosphere, and then bleeding quite a lot. At first, Tessa may be cybernetically enhanced until "Mass Destruction" cruelly subverts the ambiguous part withThe Revealthat "Tessa" is reallyCynwearing her skin.

Not bad for a man who started the day putting on the wrong biohazard suit. characters.name: Humans In General
characters.description: Ambiguous Situation: With the reveal that the Absolute Solver destroyed the Earth alongside several colonised exoplanets, and the complete absence of living humans in the present, it is unknown whether humanity as a whole was exterminated by the Solver, or if some pockets of humans survived on worlds untouched by the Solver or on space stations. Blank White Eyes: Humans seen in N's memories always sport these to contrast with the rest of their body being pitch-black. Dead All Along: If humanity was truly completely wiped out from the universe long before story really started, then they’re ultimately this just like Tessa was revealed to have been in "Mass Destruction". Endangered Species: If the humans arenotextinct, they're likely this, as many of their inhabited worlds, including Earth, were either destroyed or made uninhabitable by the Solver. The Faceless: Every human we see is either covered from head-to-toe in a protective suit with an opaque visor, or a blackened silhouette with blank white eyes. Although the silhouettes were likely a stylistic choice, completely hiding any identifying features could also have been to avoid any potentially problematicRace Tropes, as the humans on Copper 9 are all bare skeletons, and Tessa's decayed corpse cannot be pinned to any one race.

characters.name: James
characters.description: Tessa’s father, who originally owned N, V, and J back when they were Worker Drones. Abusive Parents: He is shown to look down on Worker Drones, including the ones his daughter Tessa brought into their home and was shown to allow his wife to chain up their daughter just for being friends with Worker Drones. Needless to say, both James and his wife were among the first of the Solver's victims when she slaughtered everyone at the gala. A Lighter Shade of Black:Downplayed. James is still a smug, drone-killing aristocrat who treats Worker Drones as furniture and backs the household abuse, but Louisa is the one who personally chains Tessa, tears into her in public, and banishes her Drones to the swamp. James is casually cruel and complicit but it's Louisa who is presented as the active hate sink. All There in the Script: His name only appears in the end credits. Aristocrats Are Evil: He casually murders a Worker for setting the gala tables “Western Villa style,” gossips about his own daughter as an inconvenience, and never once treats drones as people.

characters.name: Louisa
characters.description: James' wife and Tessa's mother. Abusive Parents: Verbally demeans Tessa and chains up her in her room. All There in the Script: Her name only appears in the end credits. Aristocrats Are Evil: She refers to Tessa's Drones as "dumpster pets" and refuses to let them attend the Gala, chains her own daughter for befriending servants, dumps "broken" drones in the swamp, and strings N up outside to be picked apart by crows for talking back. Asshole Victim: One of the Solver's many victims but seeing how abusive she is, she isn't likely to get sympathy points.

characters.name: Lord Frumptlebucket
characters.description: One of the many people who attend the gala. Aerith and Bob: The Aerith to Katie's Bob. Blood Knight: Enthusiastically breaks out intoYe Olde Butcherede Englishewhen watching J and V fight. The Faceless: Same as other humans in the flashbacks. One-Shot Character: Appears only in "Home".

characters.name: Katie
characters.description: One of the many people who attend the gala. Aerith and Bob: The Bob to Lord Frumptlebucket’s Aerith. The Faceless: Same as the other humans in the flashbacks. One-Shot Character: Appears only in "Home". Killed Offscreen: Is among the many casualties of the Gala Massacre, but her death isn't shown.

characters.name: Cyn
characters.description: A Worker Drone that was rescued from the dump by Tessa and was close with J, V, and particularly N. As a "Zombie Drone" that spontaneously rebooted after being improperly disposed of, Cyn was infected by the Absolute Solver, becoming its first known host and its most common avatar. Though she's nowhere to be seen in 3071, Cyn's legacy looms heavily over the events of the show. Accidental Hero: If the flashbacks inHomeare to be believed, the Gala Massacre occurred just beforeLouisa Elliotwould have had J, N, and V disposed off. Achilles' Heel: Cyn is the Solver's most powerful host, but also its primary means of interacting with reality. While losing other hosts is a minor inconvenience to it, Cyn is actually important and her destruction would cut off its ability to interact with reality. Cyn herself is nigh impossible to meaningfully damage, but her core is still vulnerable and she dies when Uzi rips it out and eats it. invokedAllegorical Character:If Cyn is a separate being from the Solver, then she could be seen as one forThe Chain of Harm. Cyn was someone who, as an expendable Worker Drone, was abandoned and abused, and after getting possessed bythe Solver, has become the abusernow finding joy in inflicting pain on others,whether they harmed her in the past like J didor even if they were once kind to her like N and Tessa. Ambiguously Evil: Very little is known about Cynwithoutthe Absolute Solver's influence/control, as she's only ever seen either as itsblatant avatar, or through itpretending to be her. On one hand, despite her "creepy" behaviour and voice, she has a genuine friendship with N, Tessa, and possibly V (at least before the Solver took stronger control), she seemingly cares about the wellbeing of the other Zombie Drones, and her playful bantering with N appears entirely wholesome.
